newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SEVEN-GOAL NEWCASTLE BACK IN TITLE HUNT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SEVEN-GOAL NEWCASTLE BACK IN TITLE HUNT.

text.p: Newcastle's title challenge was back on course on Saturday after Kevin Keegan's men thrashed Tottenham 7-1 at St James' Park to end a run of seven league games without a win.

It was Newcastle's first league triumph since they beat Middlesbrough at the beginning of November. Despite an indifferent run since then, the style and confidence they showed against Tottenham means they cannot be overlooked as serious contenders.
The rout started when Alan Shearer scored after 20 minutes and continued two minutes later when Les Ferdinand diverted home from close-range.

Tottenham, unbeaten in their previous four matches, then enjoyed their best spell of the match when they threatened to reduce the arrears, but another double goal burst midway through the second half killed them off.
Ferdinand hit the third with a volley after 59 minutes and Robert Lee made it 4-0 with a low shot that went wide of goalkeeper Ian Walker two minutes later.

Belgian international Phillipe Albert added nunber five in the 79th minute when he squeezed a low shot under Walker's body, before Shearer volleyed in a cross from David Batty eight minutes from time to make it 6-0. Lee scored his second in the 88th minute with a left-foot drive to take the tally to seven before Allan Nielsen scored a consolation for Tottenham a minute from time.

Newcastle's assistant manager Terry McDermott said: "We possibly could have got double figures today. We have had a bad run for the last month or so, but we are a good team, there is no doubt about that. Over the 90 minutes today everyone can be proud of themselves. This result could well kick-start our season."

Tottenham manager Gerry Francis, who saw his team thrashed 6-1 by first division Bolton in the League Cup a month ago, was a forlorn figure afterwards and admitted that Tottenham's day started badly when they left some of their gear behind by mistake at Stanstead Airport before their flight to Newcastle.

While Newcastle were re-establishing their credentials, champions Manchester United continued their climb up the table with a 1-0 win over Leeds at Old Trafford, their third win of the busy Christmas holiday programme.

The only goal came from former Leeds player Eric Cantona who struck home a ninth minute penalty after a sweet move between the Frenchman and Ryan Giggs was ended by Gary Kelly's illegal foul on the Welsh international.

United moved into second place above Arsenal who slipped back to third after being held to a 2-2 draw at home by Aston Villa. Arsenal led twice through Ian Wright after 13 minutes and again through Paul Merson after 73, but goals from Savo Milosevic (68) and Dwight Yorke (74) gave Villa a share of the points.

Wimbledon, whose 19-match unbeaten run was ended with a 5-0 defeat at Villa last Sunday, celebrated manager Joe Kinnear's 50th birthday with a 3-1. Everton went ahead through Wimbledon-born Graham Stuart after 23 minutes but Efan Ekoku (59), Oyvind Leonhardsen (70) and Marcus Gayle (76) replied for the Londoners who remained fourth.

Chelsea lost ground on the leading pack after racing into a 2-0 lead against Sheffield Wednesday with goals from Gianfrancola Zola -- watched by new Italian manager Cesare Maldini -- and Mark Hughes. But Wednesday came back to draw for the ninth time in 11 matches through Mark Pembridge -- with a 30 metre volley -- and Dejan Stefanovic in the last minute.
Coventry continued their climb away from the bottom with a 3-0 win over Middlesbrough -- the first time in 24 years they have won four successive league games.
But Nottingham Forest stayed bottom despite saving a point at Leicester with an 87th minute Colin Cooper goal which gave them a 2-2 draw.
